title: The router-pinned arm reads on claude-haiku-5-5, the model the haiku alias resolves to, and the pool's router record is re-run on it
goal: _tools/agent_bench.py's PIN names for haiku the model bench_core.ALIAS gives the haiku alias at the run's Claude Code version (claude-haiku-5-5 from 2.1.293), so the router-pinned arm reads on the model kb_ask.py's READER_MODEL alias runs on in use (claude -p --model haiku on this host reports modelUsage claude-haiku-5-5); one pool record of the router arm alone (run pool --arms router --reps 1, its --max-usd at 1.5x the dry run's estimate, about 6 USD) replaces the 2026-10-09 router rows and passes pool verify; benchmarks.md's pool setup text and 'What it shows', token-efficiency.md's router lines and design.md's router conclusion state the reader's model, the re-recorded cost per run and tokens per right answer, and that the earlier router rows' Haiku 4.5 reader (its 1-hour cache write at 2 USD per MTok against 0.20) is why their cost does not compare; the route-by-verdict section's setup names the reader its record ran on.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import agent_bench as a,bench_core as c;want=[m for v,m in c.ALIAS["haiku"] if v<=(2,1,293)][-1];print(a.PIN["haiku"],want);sys.exit(0 if a.PIN["haiku"]==want=="claude-haiku-5-5" else 1)
import sys;t=open("kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md",encoding="utf-8").read();bad="Haiku 4.5 reads" in t;print("Haiku 4.5 reads in benchmarks.md:",bad);sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
